newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end steady on blue chip strength.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end steady on blue chip strength.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed steady on Thursday, supported by late institutional buying of two blue chip shares, brokers siad.
The all share index closed 0.30 points higher at 558.96.
Brokers said foreign investors bought blue chip John Keells Holdings, which rose 6.25 rupees to 166.25. Commercial Leasing rose 3.25 rupees to 45 rupees.
"There is interest in John Keells because investors believe it offers very good value at current levels," said Manjula Kumarasinghe of brokerage Jardine Fleming.
Turnover was a moderate 16.24 million rupees on 648,046 shares, suported by local domestic institutional buying of 478,300 shares of Dockyard, which traded unchanged at 10.50.
"Dockyard should see good future growth due to the (goverrment's) development of Colombo Port and because it is a monopoly," said Nandakumar Nair of brokerage John Keells.
The blue chip company owns and operates dry docks and repairs quays in Colombo Port.
"A number of brokers are looking for shares, but the problem is to source quantity," Nair said.
